explanation: The UK has no specific cultural taboo against showing the soles of your feet or pointing them at someone, unlike the strong body-part taboos found in Thailand or parts of the Middle East and South Asia. The actual British faux pas is more mundane: putting your feet up on a chair, sofa, table, or train seat is seen as inconsiderate, careless of shared furniture, or unhygienic, rather than as a grave insult to another person.
local_tip: Keep your feet and shoes off seats, tables, and other furniture out of consideration for cleanliness, not because of any specific taboo about the soles themselves.

also_check.note: Feet are considered the lowest and most unclean part of the body; pointing the soles at a person or a Buddha image is genuinely offensive.
Showing the sole of your foot or shoe to someone is a real insult in much of the Arab world.
Similar to the UK, feet on furniture is seen as careless or rude in formal settings rather than taboo.
